title: Siemens digital twin targets 20% cut in hydrogen costs
html:
Siemens is working with InterContinental Energy (ICE) and Australian solution partner Mescada to develop what the companies describe as a world-first digital twin for large-scale green hydrogen production and renewable-powered AI computing. The project aims to reduce hydrogen production costs by up to 20% while accelerating the deployment of gigawatt-scale clean energy infrastructure.

For eeNews Europe readers, the project highlights the growing role of industrial simulation, digital twins and engineering software in addressing the energy demands of AI infrastructure and improving the commercial viability of green hydrogen.

Digital twins for gigawatt-scale energy projects

ICE will use Siemens’ gPROMS process modeling and COMOS engineering software to create a digital twin of its patented P2(H2)Node technology, which integrates hydrogen production with wind and solar power generation.

Each node typically combines 1 to 1.3 GW of AI computing and electrolysis capacity with around 2.6 GW of renewable energy generation.

The digital twin will allow ICE to evaluate equipment from different suppliers and test plant configurations under varying renewable energy and demand conditions before committing to construction.

“Our pioneering projects are at very large scale and in non-metro locations, so we need absolute certainty on design and cost before we commit to construction. The digital twin allows us to test technologies from different suppliers against cost and reliability targets to arrive at the optimal plant for FID. We expect this work with Siemens will deliver a cost reduction of up to 20 percent and gives us a repeatable template we can license to other developers globally. That matters well beyond our own projects, because clean energy produced at this scale can help decarbonize AI compute, steel, industry, fertilizers and shipping,” said Isaac Hinton, Head of InterContinental Energy in Australia.

Combining simulation and engineering data

The gPROMS software will serve as the process modeling engine within ICE’s Python-based optimization workflow, while COMOS will manage engineering data, equipment specifications and technical documentation.

“Energy at this scale can only be built with confidence if projects can be designed, tested and costed digitally before construction starts. ICE is among a growing wave of energy developers that want a digital twin from the earliest feasibility stage, rather than waiting until the build or operations, and gPROMS and COMOS give them a single, trusted source of engineering and cost data to do that. This project is a great example of collaboration between Siemens, Mescada and ICE to deliver a world-first solution,” said Darryl Kaufmann, Managing Director of Digital Industries at Siemens Australia and New Zealand.

Scaling through industry partnerships

The Australian Renewable Energy Agency (ARENA) is contributing A$1.56 million to the A$3.12 million project. Mescada will coordinate software delivery, training and technical support.

“As a long-standing Siemens solution partner in Australia, our job is to ensure customers get the full value of the technology from day one. For ICE, that has meant bringing gPROMS and COMOS together so that process modelling, engineering data and cost information sit in a single source of truth, backed by hands-on training and ongoing support. GW scale energy still a new frontier for all of us, and it is rewarding to see ICE secure ARENA funding and put Siemens technology at the center of how it plans to scale,” said Hung Chan, CEO of Mescada.
